Scenario fixture: password-paste-enabled

Each target has a stable id of the form ppe_case_NN. A paste handler attached with addEventListener is not represented: it leaves no trace in the markup, so no static page can demonstrate that branch. The rule is advisory and never reports a failure, so every case here is either raised for review or left alone.

A. Cancelling is the whole handler (CANTTELL)

01 — CANTTELL: password field whose inline handler returns false
02 — CANTTELL: password field whose inline handler calls preventDefault
03 — CANTTELL: one-time-code field, reached through autocomplete rather than input type
04 — CANTTELL: new-password field setting returnValue

B. The handler does more than cancel (CANTTELL)

05 — CANTTELL: inline handler delegates to a function, so whether it cancels is not in the markup
09 — CANTTELL: cancels the default and then re-inserts the trimmed text, which helps rather than blocks
10 — CANTTELL: split one-time-code field distributing the pasted digits across its boxes
11 — CANTTELL: cancels only under a condition, so it does not always block

C. Nothing to review

06 — NEUTRAL: password field with no paste handler, so nothing to review
07 — NEUTRAL: autocomplete="off" is not reported, since browsers override it for password managers

D. Out of scope

08 — NEUTRAL: an ordinary text field is not an authentication field, whatever it does with paste
12 — NEUTRAL: type="password" masking a card security code, which is not an authentication secret
13 — NEUTRAL: a disabled field takes no input, so there is no paste to block
14 — NEUTRAL: a readonly field takes no input either

End of fixture.
